How to stop spam from filling your inbox

Spam filters work best when you train them. Mark unwanted messages as spam instead of simply deleting them, and the filter learns the pattern over time. Unsubscribe from newsletters you no longer read, since each one you keep adds to the pile.

You can safely ignore promotional emails from shops you have never used. Most of them stop after a few weeks without any engagement from you. Avoid clicking links in messages you did not expect, even if they look official, and never enter a password through a link in an email. If the same sender keeps getting through, add the address to your blocked list.

For a clean start, create a separate address for online sign-ups. Keep your main address for friends, family, and banking. Review your filter settings once a month to catch any legitimate messages that were sent to the wrong folder.

Passage 14. Prompt engineering refers to the practice of writing instructions that guide a language model toward a useful output. Developers often write system prompts that set tone and constraints, then add a few examples to show the expected format. Researchers also study prompt injection, where untrusted text inside a document attempts to override the instructions the developer wrote. Common defenses include separating data from instructions, limiting what tools a model can call, and validating outputs before they are shown to a user. Rinse one cup of red lentils and add them to four cups of stock with a diced onion, two carrots, and a teaspoon of cumin. Simmer for 25 minutes, until the lentils break down.
